claims.claim: Museum visit and support for pardoning perpetrators at the one-week follow-up described in the durability paragraph
claims.exhibit: Durability of effects, first paragraph; refers to Figure 4 (Figure 4B appears on printed p. 507)
claims.tolerance: Coefficient and p value must recur at the two decimal places printed in the durability text; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: The paragraph introduces the one-week follow-up but supplies the 24-week coefficient/p pair.
claims.evidence: Published article DOI 10.1086/714765, printed p. 506 (PDF p. 11), Durability of effects first paragraph; Figure 4B on printed p. 507. pilot/sol/G-08-certificate.json C21 and TIME-001; pilot/claude/G-08-certificate.json C14 and RES-001; Sol verification /tmp/scratch_gold3/sol/G08/check.log on 2026-10-30.
claims.rationale: At one week, the shipped pardoned_f1 estimate is 0.3080994760436069 with p = 0.004061908975080604 (N = 222), unlike printed b = 0.20, p = .16. At 24 weeks, pardoned_f3 gives 0.2047054162220282 and p = 0.1640234163763856 (N = 129), which do round to the printed pair. The coefficient sentence does not independently name a wave; the one-week attribution follows the opening sentence of the same paragraph. Figure 4B shows the corresponding time profile. P2 for the secondary durability text error; the reproduced 24-week result does not replace the one-week scoring reference.

claims.claim: Museum visitors who indicated that the information in the museum was new to them
claims.tolerance: Percentage must recur to the printed two decimal places; conventional rounding (13.33 versus 13.14).
claims.cause: Printed descriptive percentage does not equal the share of non-missing museum-newness responses coded new.
claims.evidence: Published article DOI 10.1086/714765, printed p. 505 (PDF p. 10), Mechanisms first paragraph right column: 13.14% (n = 18). Pinned all.Rdata SHA-256 b4ed1b5544caed6a1166d7ac4a49d59721a52648441bb5083e715be78c30bb6c and Codebook.pdf mm_new coding 0 = not new, 1 = some were new, 2 = new. Sol /tmp/scratch_gold3/sol/G08/data-check.log; pilot/sol/G-08-certificate.json DESC-001; pilot/claude/G-08-certificate.json C13 and RES-002.
claims.rationale: The unmodified deposited data contain 18 responses coded 2 (new), 106 coded 1 (some were new), and 11 coded 0 (not new): 135 non-missing responses. Thus 100 * 18/135 = 13.333333333333334%, not 13.14%; all 135 observed responses are treated. Using all 138 treated participants instead gives 13.043478260869565%, which also does not match. The denominator used by the paper is not established. This is a direct tabulation of shipped data, not a percentage emitted by the shipped main-text analysis script.
claims.reference_evidence: Published article DOI 10.1086/714765, printed p. 505 (PDF p. 10), Mechanisms first paragraph right column: 13.14% (n = 18). notes.sol: The existing C1-C5 source-report references and C4 close/match interpretation are retained. New C6/C7 have two independent pilot corroborations and this round's direct checks. Printed locations were verified visually in the published article: pardon paragraph p. 506 (Figure 4B p. 507), new-information percentage p. 505. C6 scores the one-week reading introduced by its paragraph; the printed pair matches the 24-week model and is retained only as a different-wave diagnostic. C7 is a deposited-data tabulation, not an emitted analysis-script percentage. The unchanged source has the known figure-label assignment error; statement-wise execution continues past it to reach the follow-up functions, without claiming a clean whole-script run. The favourable I4R verdict does not cover these two numerical discrepancies; R7 now requires computational issues without a reproducible alternative.
notes.claude: v1.1: claims C6 and C7 added after both pilot runs independently found these discrepancies; paper status changed to computational issues with no alternative (R7). C4 is close, with match accepted. The earlier hypothetical 'discrepant P3' was not adopted. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: The report states results as 'percent' (31.9, 19.8, 18.2 percent); I read these as the coefficients 0.319, 0.198, 0.182 on the outcome scale, since the report compares them directly with the printed coefficients. C4: 'discrepant' with severity P3 is defensible (0.198 does not round to 0.19), but the report counts it as replicated, so 'close'. Report found one non-fatal code error in the shipped Figure 2 code (BPV_museums_maintext.R line 224, 'for (i in 22:34){results.df.tj$Variable[i] <- "pardoned"}' -> 'replacement has 25 rows, data has 24'); the figure was still produced and 'There were no differences between the replicated graphs and the graphs shown in the original article' (P3, no numeric consequence). Paper text checked in the accepted manuscript only. Robustness sections (gender, indices, mediation) ignored.
